Model registry

Every model version, and why it changed

Only registered model versions publish numbers. Each version’s file is recorded in the registry with its SHA-256 hash, so any change to a model shows, and every promotion and retirement is listed with its reason.

Models publishing now

Read from the test results bound to each published file.

Earthquake: S1 (C0 + GEAR1)

Combines where large earthquakes happen in the long run with how they cluster after recent ones, plus GEAR1’s long-term rate from crustal strain. On 2023–2025 (a second look at those years), it ranked a cell that went on to have an M6+ earthquake above one that did not 97% of the time across the globe, and 77% among cells with recent earthquakes, the harder question.

Hurricane: NOAA DTOPS, and v8.2 elsewhere

For storms the National Hurricane Center covers, we publish NOAA’s own DTOPS guidance: in a test written down in advance and run once on the 2025 season it beat NOAA SHIPS-RII, NOAA RIOC consensus and our previous model (v8.2), ranking a forecast cycle that went on to intensify rapidly above one that did not 93% of the time. Elsewhere we publish our v8.2 model. Beside it, our satellite model J1 is recorded and, for West Pacific and South Indian storms, shown while it is tested on new forecasts. Our v10.1 model is shown beside DTOPS, labelled experimental, while it is tested on new forecasts. Our track and intensity forecast, TC1, is shown beside NHC’s official forecast.

Tornado: v3

Scores every thunderstorm NOAA tracks over the contiguous US for the chance it produces a tornado in the next hour. On every storm of 2025, scored once, it ranked a storm that went on to produce a tornado above one that did not 97% of the time.

Every version in use

Published: produces the number on the site. Fallback: takes over when an input feed is down. Experimental: shown beside the published number while it is tested on new forecasts. Shadow: recorded on every live forecast and never shown as one; listed here when its test could change what is published.

How a model is promoted

  • A candidate is compared with the published model in a test written down before the deciding data is scored, on the same cases, with paired intervals.
  • It is promoted only if the test’s own rule says it is better; a gain whose interval includes zero is not enough.
  • The promoted file is frozen and named by its hash. Its live forecasts are recorded and scored from the moment it publishes.
  • A retired model’s past forecasts stay in the ledger and in its live record on the track record.
